text:
Colten Ellis stopped all 23 shots he saw, and the Sabres snapped a three-game winless run (0-1-2) with a 2-0 win in San Jose. Ellis was a 93rd overall pick by the Blues in 2019 who spent last season in the AHL with Springfield, and his night looks even bigger in our numbers. Goals saved above expected, which measures how many more goals a goalie stopped than the chances he faced should have produced, put him at 3.0 for the game.

The game was closer than the score, and Buffalo still held the edge. Expected goals, which weigh the quality of every shot, favored BUF 4.78 to 3.02, and in a simulation of replays of every shot, BUF wins that matchup 64 percent of the time. The Sabres outshot the Sharks 40 to 23. Yaroslav Askarov, the 11th overall pick in 2020, kept San Jose in it with 38 saves, about 2.9 goals better than expected, and the Sharks were hurt by 21 giveaways against Buffalo's 6.

Olen Zellweger broke it open early in the second period with a snap shot that had only a 4 percent chance of going in, the least likely goal of the night. Zach Benson sealed it at 19:05 of the third on a wrist shot rated 89 percent. For Buffalo, the shutout ends a rough stretch. San Jose, which went 0 for 3 on the power play, will have to find a way to turn its work into shots on goal.
